scope: Theorem 5.1 (Rounding a grid solution) of the manuscript “The approximation threshold for metric k-median” (preprints/The-Approximation-Threshold-for-Metric-k-Median-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 125 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c8176d1671beb83d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 16-17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed τ > 0 and all sufficiently large constant integers ∆, put g = 1/∆. Suppose a finite rational metric instance has openings ̃ yi ∈ [0, 1] ∩ gZ of total mass M ≥ 1. For a client j, let Vj,0 be the cost of its nearest unit of this mass. There is a 16 constant C = C(τ, ∆) and a randomized algorithm of expected polynomial running time that outputs a set O of facilities with |O| ≤ M + C, Ed(j, O) ≤ (1 + 2/e + τ)Vj,0 for every client j. All parameters and the additive constant are independent of the instance. In particular, an initial mass at most k + c0, for a fixed constant c0, gives at most k + c0 + C facilities. The deterministic implementation of the resulting total-cost guarantee is given in Section 6.
